simple: Advertising where you pay only when a specific measurable action happens (like a click, lead, or sale).
example: A salon paying ₹50 only when a customer books an appointment online.

simple: The journey a customer takes from first seeing your brand to finally making a purchase.
example: 1,000 see your ad → 100 click → 20 enquire → 5 buy.

simple: The key action you want someone to take on your website or ad.
example: A customer clicking 'Book Consultation' or buying a saree.

simple: The total number of times your ad was displayed on screen.
example: If Priya sees your ad 3 times, that counts as 3 impressions.

simple: The number of unique individual people who saw your ad at least once.
example: If Priya sees your ad 3 times, reach is 1.

simple: Average number of times each person saw your ad (Impressions ÷ Reach).
example: 10,000 impressions ÷ 5,000 people reached = frequency of 2.0.

simple: Cost to show your ad 1,000 times to your audience.
example: If you spend ₹150 to get 1,000 views, your CPM is ₹150.

simple: Percentage of people who clicked your ad after seeing it.
example: 100 clicks from 5,000 impressions = 2% CTR.

simple: The average amount you pay each time someone clicks your ad.
example: Spent ₹500 for 50 clicks → CPC is ₹10.

simple: The amount you spend to acquire one customer contact enquiry or lead.
example: Spent ₹2,000 and received 40 WhatsApp enquiries → CPL is ₹50.

simple: The cost to acquire one paying customer or completed transaction.
example: Spent ₹3,000 for 6 gym annual memberships → CPA is ₹500.

simple: Percentage of visitors who take the desired final action.
example: 50 leads out of 500 website clicks = 10% CVR.

simple: Revenue generated divided by ad spend. Measures profitability.
example: Generated ₹40,000 revenue from ₹10,000 ad spend = 4.0x ROAS.

simple: The top level of Meta ad setup where you choose your ultimate business objective.
example: Setting up a 'Leads' campaign for Diwali festive sales.

simple: The middle level of setup where you define who (audience), where (placements), and budget.
example: Targeting women aged 25-45 in Bengaluru on Instagram Reels.

simple: The actual visual and text that users see on their screen.
example: A 15-second customer testimonial video with an offer headline.

simple: A tiny piece of code on your website that tracks actions visitors take.
example: Tells Meta whenever a visitor adds an item to cart or buys.

simple: Direct server-to-server connection that sends events safely even if browser ad-blockers are active.
example: Your Shopify server notifying Meta directly when an order is paid.

simple: A score from 0-10 measuring how accurately customer data matches Meta user profiles.
example: Sending email and phone number with an event gives an EMQ of 8.5/10.

simple: An audience of people who have already interacted with your business.
example: People who visited your salon's website in the last 30 days.

simple: Meta finding new people who resemble your best existing customers.
example: 1% Lookalike of your top 500 paying customers in India.

simple: Targeting with no detailed interest or behavior filters, letting Meta AI find the buyers.
example: Targeting all adults 21-55 in Delhi NCR with an open interest setting.

simple: Narrowing your audience based on interests, demographics, or behaviors.
example: Targeting people interested in 'Yoga' and 'Organic Food'.

simple: Meta's automated AI campaign for e-commerce that optimizes targeting and placements automatically.
example: An apparel brand running one ASC campaign across all of India.

simple: The initial period after launch when Meta AI experiments to find the best buyers.
example: Needs ~50 conversions per ad set in 7 days to exit learning.

simple: When an ad set fails to get 50 conversions in a week, resulting in higher and unstable costs.
example: An ad set getting only 8 leads a week gets stuck in Learning Limited.

simple: A form that opens instantly inside Facebook or Instagram without leaving the app.
example: A 2-field form asking for name and mobile number that auto-fills.

simple: An ad that opens a direct WhatsApp chat with your business when tapped.
example: A local clinic ad: 'Chat with our doctor on WhatsApp'.

simple: The average amount you are willing to spend per day on an ad set or campaign.
example: Setting ₹500/day for a continuous 30-day run.

simple: A fixed total budget spent across the entire scheduled duration of a campaign.
example: ₹15,000 total budget for a 10-day Diwali clearance sale.

simple: The real-time bidding process Meta runs to decide which ad gets shown on a user's feed.
example: Based on Bid × Estimated Action Rate × Ad Quality.

simple: Meta's prediction of how likely a specific person is to convert on your ad.
example: If Meta predicts high intent, your effective bid increases for free.

simple: Meta's score based on user feedback, clickbait absence, and watch time.
example: Ads with high engagement and zero hidden costs get lower CPMs.

simple: Default bidding where Meta spends your full budget to get the maximum possible results.
example: Meta automatically bids whatever is needed to get 30 leads today.

simple: Setting a ceiling on the average cost per result Meta is allowed to charge you.
example: Telling Meta: 'Do not get leads if the average cost exceeds ₹120'.

simple: The maximum amount you are willing to bid in any individual ad auction.
example: Capping individual bids at ₹15 per click.

simple: When your audience has seen your ad so many times that CTR drops and costs spike.
example: Frequency reaches 4.8 and CPL jumps from ₹60 to ₹180.

simple: The opening visual and audio of a video ad designed to stop someone scrolling.
example: 'Stop washing your hair with hot water!' in the first 2 seconds.

simple: The button or instruction prompting the user what to do next.
example: 'Book Now', 'Learn More', or 'Send WhatsApp Message'.

simple: Authentic video or photos created by real customers or creators using your product.
example: An unboxing video recorded on a mobile phone looking natural.

simple: An ad format with 2 to 10 swipeable images or videos, each with its own link.
example: Showing 5 best-selling kurta designs in one swipeable post.

simple: Comparing two versions of an ad changing only ONE variable to see which performs better.
example: Testing Video Hook A vs Video Hook B with identical copy and audience.

simple: When two of your ad sets target the same people, causing them to bid against each other.
example: Targeting 'Fitness' in Ad Set 1 and 'Gym' in Ad Set 2 with 60% identical users.

simple: Removing a specific group of people from your ad targeting to avoid wasting money.
example: Excluding people who already bought in the last 30 days.

simple: Showing ads specifically to people who previously engaged or visited your website.
example: Showing a 10% discount ad to people who abandoned their cart.

simple: Reaching completely cold audiences who have never heard of your brand before.
example: A broad educational video introducing a new skincare routine.

simple: Nurturing interested prospects who know your brand but haven't purchased yet.
example: Sharing customer reviews and doctor certifications with page engagers.

simple: Closing high-intent prospects ready to buy right now with an irresistible offer.
example: A limited-time coupon ad targeted at cart abandoners.

simple: Increasing the budget of an existing winning ad set or campaign by ~20% at a time.
example: Raising daily budget from ₹1,000 to ₹1,200 every 2-3 days.

simple: Scaling by finding new audiences, testing new creative angles, or duplicating winners into new targets.
example: Testing a new 2% Lookalike audience and a broader interest group.

simple: The time period after a click or view during which Meta counts a conversion.
example: 7-day click or 1-day view attribution.

simple: When someone buys after merely seeing your ad without clicking it within 24 hours.
example: A user sees your ad on Instagram, then opens browser and buys directly.

simple: Measuring whether an ad actually caused a purchase that wouldn't have happened otherwise.
example: Checking if turning off branded ads decreases total sales.

simple: The central hub for managing your Meta ad accounts, pages, pixels, and team permissions.
example: An agency managing 10 client accounts under one dashboard.

simple: The specific account inside Business Manager that holds your campaigns and billing details.
example: The ad account where you add your GST number and credit card.

simple: Entering your 18% GST number in Meta billing to claim input tax credits in India.
example: Claiming ₹1,800 input credit on a ₹10,000 Meta ad bill.

simple: Meta automatically enhancing your ad images with lighting, music, and text combinations.
example: Meta automatically applying subtle brightness boost and 3D tilt.

simple: Uploading multiple images, copy lines, and headlines so Meta mixes and matches them for each user.
example: Uploading 3 videos, 2 copies, and 2 headlines to let Meta find the best combo.

simple: The central area of a 9:16 vertical video where text is not covered by UI icons or captions.
example: Keeping your offer text away from the bottom 20% and right edge.

simple: The still preview image shown before a video starts playing.
example: A high-contrast still with an intriguing question text overlay.

simple: Evidence that others trust and love your product (reviews, ratings, press logos).
example: 'Over 10,000 happy brides across India' badge in your ad image.

simple: A free valuable resource given in exchange for contact info.
example: A free 'Diwali Home Decor Guide PDF' in exchange for name and WhatsApp.

simple: Connecting your lead ad directly to your sales software or Google Sheets in real-time.
example: Sending a new lead to the telecaller's phone in under 60 seconds.

simple: How quickly your sales team calls a lead after they submit the ad form.
example: Calling within 5 minutes results in 4x higher conversion than calling next day.

simple: The average rupee amount spent each time a customer places an order.
example: Total sales ₹50,000 ÷ 25 orders = ₹2,000 AOV.

simple: Total marketing and sales spend required to acquire a brand-new customer.
example: Spent ₹20,000 on ads to acquire 20 new customers = ₹1,000 CAC.

simple: Total profit or revenue a customer brings over their entire relationship with you.
example: A salon customer visiting once a month for a year brings ₹18,000 LTV.

simple: Comparison of customer value to acquisition cost; healthy businesses aim for 3:1.
example: ₹3,000 lifetime value vs ₹1,000 acquisition cost.

simple: How fast, clear, and trustworthy your destination website is after a click.
example: A mobile page that loads in 1.5 seconds with clear ₹ prices and UPI checkout.

simple: Tags added to your website URL to track where traffic came from in analytics tools.
example: utm_source=facebook&utm_medium=cpc&utm_campaign=summer_sale.

simple: Information you collect directly from your audience (emails, phone numbers, past orders).
example: Your shop's loyalty customer list of 2,000 phone numbers.

simple: When an ad is rejected for violating Meta guidelines (sensational claims, before/after body shots).
example: Promising 'Lose 10kg in 3 days' will trigger an immediate ban.

simple: When Meta temporarily disables an ad account due to policy strikes or suspicious billing.
example: Account paused until you verify identity with PAN or business documents.

simple: Setting one budget at campaign level and letting Meta allocate it among ad sets.
example: ₹3,000/day distributed automatically to whichever ad set performs best today.

simple: Setting individual fixed budgets at the ad set level for strict control.
example: Forcing exactly ₹500 to Ad Set 1 and ₹500 to Ad Set 2.

simple: Segmenting ad results by age, gender, placement, device, or region.
example: Discovering that 80% of your leads came from Instagram Reels on Android.

simple: How far back Meta looks at user actions when creating custom audiences.
example: People who added to cart in the past 14 days vs 180 days.

simple: The underlying psychological appeal or perspective used to sell a product.
example: Angle 1: Save time. Angle 2: Save money. Angle 3: Look stylish.

simple: Creators with 5k-50k followers creating relatable ad content for brands.
example: A college student showing how she packs her lunchbox for the day.

simple: The percentage of subscribers or customers who stop buying over a given period.
example: A subscription box losing 5 out of 100 subscribers per month = 5% churn.
